[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Building Sequential Workflows with Pipeline in Scikit-learn"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In machine learning workflows, data preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training are rarely performed in isolation. Instead, they form a sequential pipeline where the output of one step serves as the input to the next. Scikit-learn provides the Pipeline class to encapsulate these sequential steps, ensuring reproducibility, preventing data leakage, and simplifying the model evaluation process."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Why Use a Pipeline?"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Convenience and encapsulation: You only need to call fit and predict once on your combined data to chain all the estimators."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Joint parameter tuning: You can grid search over hyperparameters of all steps in the pipeline at the same time."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prevention of data leakage: Transformers inside the pipeline are fitted only on the training folds of cross-validation splits, preventing validation data from biasing the preprocessing steps."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Basic Pipeline"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To create a pipeline, you supply a list of tuples. Each tuple contains a string name for the step and an instance of a transformer or estimator object. The final step must be an estimator (such as a classifier or regressor)."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.svm import SVC

# Construct the pipeline with scaling and classification steps
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
    ('classifier', SVC())
])"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Fitting and Evaluating the Pipeline"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once constructed, the pipeline object exposes the standard scikit-learn estimator interface. When you call fit, the pipeline calls fit_transform on each transformer in turn, transforming the input and passing it to the next step, culminating in the fit method of the final estimator."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer

# Load dataset and split into train and test sets
data = load_breast_cancer()
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    data.data, data.target, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
)

# Fit the pipeline on the training data
pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predict and evaluate on the test data
accuracy = pipeline.score(X_test, y_test)
print("Test Accuracy: {:.4f}".format(accuracy))"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Accessing Pipeline Steps"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can access individual steps within a pipeline using dictionary indexing or via the named_steps attribute. This is useful when you want to inspect learned parameters, such as feature importances or scaling means."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# Accessing the fitted scaler step
scaler_step = pipeline.named_steps['scaler']
print("Mean values of features:", scaler_step.mean_)"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Hyperparameter Tuning with GridSearchCV"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pipelines integrate seamlessly with hyperparameter search tools like GridSearchCV. To tune parameters of specific steps in the pipeline, prefix the parameter name with the step name followed by a double underscore."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV

# Define the parameter grid using step__parameter syntax
param_grid = {
    'classifier__C': [0.1, 1, 10, 100],
    'classifier__kernel': ['linear', 'rbf']
}

# Set up GridSearchCV with the pipeline
grid_search = GridSearchCV(pipeline, param_grid, cv=5)
grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)

print("Best Parameters:", grid_search.best_params_)"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Scikit-learn Pipeline class is an essential tool for building robust, clean, and production-ready machine learning architectures. By grouping data transformations and model training into a single entity, you eliminate common bugs related to data leakage and ensure seamless end-to-end execution."}]
